blocks.text: Model the composer and current turn explicitly. Persisted unsent text, transient IME interaction, attachment work, a pending send command, the optimistic message, and sequenced assistant output have different lifetimes and failure paths.

ComposerDraft is scoped by account and conversation and stores recoverable text, never transient IME state. ComposerInteractionState remains in memory while the control is mounted. AttachmentDraft tracks local upload readiness. PendingSend correlates the optimistic user message. StreamMessage accepts deltas only from its stream identity and next sequence.

State-model checks:
- Draft revision and transient IME composition are explicit but separate.
- Attachment readiness cannot be inferred from a URL.
- Client message and command IDs make uncertain send retry idempotent.
- Stream identity and sequence reject stale or duplicate deltas.

blocks.title: State checkpoint
blocks.text: The model is trustworthy when unsent intent, attachment readiness, send acknowledgement, and assistant streaming cannot overwrite one another.

Keep ComposerDraft, ComposerInteractionState, AttachmentDraft, and PendingSend separate from conversation messages. Persist the draft by account and conversation, but keep IME composition state transient because it belongs to the mounted control. A sent user message gets a client ID for idempotent reconciliation. Streaming assistant text is a sequenced message resource, while the local composer draft can persist independently across navigation.
